decision: A pharmacy bill gets its PHI number when it is first posted (checkout, draft finish or status change), reserved on the posting transaction; drafts hold a DRAFT- placeholder that no screen, print, search or API shows as a number

evidence: pharmacy-bill-discounts.database.spec.ts: three drafts, middle discarded, two finished plus a new bill and two concurrent bills number 001 to 005 with no gap; a forced failure after numbering consumed none

decision: Rejected: a nullable bill number for drafts
why: about 30 readers join on invoiceNumber and build INV-<number> stock references in template strings, which accept null silently, so the compiler would not find them; the NOT NULL unique key keeps every join total

decision: Drafts saved before this change keep the number they already reserved and finishing fills it; discarding one of those still leaves its gap
why: renumbering them would change numbers staff may already have written down; the data model allows any number of such drafts, and the Sales day-wise report lists their numbers as unissued with their status

decision: A draft cannot be printed: Print and PDF are disabled for drafts in Sales and the invoice list, and the server refuses print data for an unfinished bill; the builder's print preview of an unsaved bill says the number is given when the bill is printed

decision: A bill's date becomes the moment it is numbered

decision: Pricing rule in whole paise: line discount, then the bill discount split across lines in proportion to each line's value after its own discount by largest remainder (ties to the earlier line), then tax on the line's discounted value; bill figures are sums of line figures

evidence: bill-pricing.spec.ts literal 3 lines 5/12/18% with 10% and ₹50; frontend parity test runs the server module

decision: The bill stores the discount as typed (kind and value), its rupee amount, and each line's share; discountAmount becomes item plus bill discount

evidence: pharmacy-bill-discounts.database.spec.ts print data and return line values

decision: Known gap: a sales return saved at the same moment as a discount change is not serialized against it; the return may freeze the pre-change terms

decision: Every reader that adds up a pharmacy bill's money uses one ledger rule (COMPLETED receipts plus REFUNDED negative entries) from pharmacy-ledger.ts; the daily collection books a bill refund in the Refunds column of the mode and day it was handed back

decision: The known gap above does not hold: a discount edit and a sales return are both serializable transactions with retries, so PostgreSQL aborts one of a crossing pair; the edit is then refused or the return re-reads the revised terms

decision: A discount edit rewrites return terms per sold unit and is refused with a plain message when a return could not tell which price applies (one drug at different unit prices on the bill, or a sold batch now linked to several drugs)

decision: Payment needs an issued bill number as well as a non-draft status; refund request keys are stored as refund:<key> beside payment keys

decision: Mark as paid in the invoice list collects what the ledger leaves due (settlementOf, receipts less refunds)

decision: Open for the clinic: a discount edit that raises a paid bill's total leaves it due, and a sales return before that due is collected refunds the full revised value

decision: Below a 72rem container each medicine is a compact row from the same table markup, with no per-field labels. From 32rem (the 1280 laptop, about 530px) line 1 is Medicine, Frequency and When, and line 2 is Duration, the full Instructions and icon-only add-below and remove buttons, under one two-line column header shown once above the list; the stock hint sits on the name field's top border. Under 32rem (phones) a row is medicine; frequency and when; duration with the buttons; instructions, with headers left to placeholders (Frequency, When) and accessible names (Frequency for <medicine>, When for <medicine>, Duration unit for <medicine>, Remove <medicine>). From 72rem up it is a fixed table: Frequency 8.75rem, When 11.25rem, Duration 10.5rem, Actions 6rem, and Instructions takes the rest. The Rx tables opt out of the global main th/td padding (data-own-cell-spacing)
why: the doctors asked for column widths, not a different layout, and the labelled card made one medicine 299px tall at 1280 and 591px at 390. The brief put Duration and the buttons on line 1, but at 530px that left Medicine about 40px, so Duration and the buttons move to line 2: Instructions still gets 266px, wider than the 256px the clinic's '1 pea size amount- whole face' needs, and focus order matches reading order. Track widths come from measured text in the app font so 'Frequency', 'Empty Stomach' and 'MONTHS' stay on one line. The unlayered global rule padding: 0.75rem 1rem on every th and td in main overrode every Tailwind padding in these tables and was most of the height. Rows are separated by a divider and zebra. The template editor uses the same rows
evidence: PrescriptionBuilder.rx-table jest (names of every control, header row once, remove from the middle; both failed on the card markup); stack scenario 19-* row heights 1280 <=96px (93px) and 390 <=170px (168px), headers once at 1280, Tab order at 1280, no clipping, no sideways scroll; 19-template row heights

decision: Rows and draft lines separate paid and free units; free units go on the CR-27 return line's freeQuantity at no value; group value and the minimum count paid units; a partial return takes units in the bill's remaining paid-to-free ratio, rounding toward free

decision: Create return draft runs the classification and the write in one Serializable transaction under an advisory lock per branch and distributor; a second press with a different key sees the first draft and is refused with "Every batch is already on a return draft"

evidence: DB spec two concurrent presses -> one draft (fails without the lock)

phase: review fix payment status at creation

why: the desk has the money in hand, so the revenue report, the payment summary, refunds and Daily Collection must all see it; keeping desk payments PENDING was rejected because only COMPLETED payments count as revenue and refunds refuse anything else
evidence: payment-status DB spec desk/gateway/confirm-twice; stack cr17-appointment-billing

phase: review fix received equals completed payments
decision: invoice.received moves only with COMPLETED payments and refunds; Daily Collection's clinic block reads COMPLETED payments only; existing PENDING rows are left as they are (no backfill migration)
why: one rule for every money surface; no backfill because before CR-17 the desk payment route refused every CUID bill, so no desk payment can be PENDING in a live clinic
evidence: payment-status DB spec revenue vs Daily Collection literal totals

phase: review fix payment cap and races
decision: The server refuses an amount at or below 0 and an amount above the bill's balance with 400 naming the due; the balance check and the write are one conditional UPDATE inside the payment transaction; refunds use the same conditional update on received; confirming a gateway payment that no longer fits the balance is refused with 409 and stays PENDING
why: a conditional update was chosen over Serializable plus retries because the single row lock already orders racing writers with no retry loop; bulk payments now run in one transaction so a refusal leaves no half-paid batch
evidence: payment-status DB spec concurrent pair and concurrent refunds; billing.rules spec overpay

phase: review fix dialog after a refused payment

why: the refusal usually means someone else took the money; making the user close and reopen to see it was rejected
evidence: DoctorDayCalendar.billing spec refusal test; stack cr17 refusal screenshots

decision: A prescription line's product is the drug its stocked item links, else its standard name ignoring case and spacing; lines that share a linked drug, a batch id or a name join one product, and two different linked drugs never join; names no longer match by substring
why: inventoryItemId is a batch row, so keying on it lost history when the oldest batch was archived and split name-only lines from id lines; keying on the name alone was rejected because a renamed item's old lines only connect through their batch id
evidence: prescription-learning.test batch A/B and name-only cases; contracts test Cetirizine/Levocetirizine now a pass claim

decision: The agent's output schema gains itemNaming (form enum, medicineName, strength, isCombination) and its instructions say how to fill it; when the model leaves the form out the recorded-name parser reads it from the proposed name; when neither gives a form, name and strength the proposal is not staged and the agent's reply asks for what is missing

decision: A calendar row keeps, left to right: token, its own time range, the patient name (truncates first, full name in the row's label and tooltip), bill type, status and the bill chip, on one line inside its slot (20px for 15 minutes at 900px tall). why: the lead's target: time, a readable name, type, status and chip on every desktop row without growing the row; 1280 rows showed '#4 Pri...' because the chip took the time's room. Lead decision 3 prefers words where they fit: measured at 1280 with the app's 14px row text, a 16-character name, token, time, bill type and a word badge do not fit beside a due chip, so the dot is used there and words from 1440
evidence: CalendarColumn.tsx; cr17 row geometry scenarios at 1280, 1440 and 390

decision: The bill chip's wording steps up with the block's width: a phone row says ₹✓ or ₹!, a narrow row (12rem) Paid or ₹200 due, a desktop row (24rem, both 1280 and 1440) ₹500 · Paid or ₹200 due, a full row (38rem) the total and bill count (₹1,700 · ₹200 due · 2 bills); a bill with nothing received never repeats its sum (₹1,700 due).
